title: Puy lentil salad with radishes and orange

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain whole food or a cupboard staple: lentils, oranges, oil, mustard, onion, radishes, watercress, walnuts and parsley.

supermarket.reason: Puy lentils, watercress, walnuts and radishes are all everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, sieve, bowl and whisk, and the techniques are simmering, slicing and whisking.

works.reason: 250g puy lentils simmered for 20 minutes with 300g radishes, oranges, watercress and walnuts makes a sound, well-dressed lunch for four, though the juice caught from slicing the oranges is only just enough for 4 tbsp oil.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for peeling and slicing the oranges, radishes and onion and making the dressing, and the 30 cook minutes match the 20-minute simmer plus 10 minutes cooling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the parsley, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted except water is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A substantial 300g of radishes with watercress and the last oranges suits a mid-April lunch, and the radishes carry the salad.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, walnuts and plenty of vegetables and fruit make a filling, real-food lunch a family would make again.
